lines.text: Why does GameStop pay so little for your old games?
lines.say: Why does GameStop pay so little for your old games?

lines.text: GameStop's own annual report once spelled it out.
lines.say: GameStop's own annual report once spelled it out.

lines.text: In fiscal 2018, used and value products kept 43.4% as gross profit; new consoles, 8.5%.
lines.say: In fiscal twenty eighteen, used and value products kept about forty-three percent as gross profit; new consoles, eight and a half.

lines.text: That's about 5 times the margin, on mostly traded-in stock.
lines.say: That's about five times the margin, on mostly traded-in stock.

lines.text: Our math: $100 of those sales left about $43 of gross profit.
lines.say: Our math: a hundred dollars of those sales left about forty-three dollars of gross profit.

lines.text: That spread also pays for stores, staff, testing, and games nobody buys.
lines.say: That spread also pays for stores, staff, testing, and games nobody buys.

lines.text: In the quarter to August 1, 2026, pre-owned and refurbished sales were $170.7 million, 21.6% of sales.
lines.say: In the quarter to August first, twenty twenty-six, pre-owned and refurbished sales were about a hundred seventy-one million, about a fifth of sales.

lines.text: Total sales fell from $6.01 billion in fiscal 2021 to $3.63 billion in fiscal 2025.
lines.say: Total sales fell from about six billion in fiscal twenty twenty-one to about three point six billion in fiscal twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: So a trade-in quote is a reseller's buying price, not your game's worth.
lines.say: So a trade-in quote is a reseller's buying price, not your game's worth.

post.title: Why GameStop pays so little for your trade-ins
post.ig:
Why does GameStop pay so little for your old games?
In fiscal 2018, GameStop's 10-K showed a 43.4% gross margin on pre-owned and value products versus 8.5% on new video game hardware.
Our math: on $100 of those sales, about $43 was gross profit, before stores, staff and unsold stock.
In the quarter ended Aug 1, 2026, pre-owned and refurbished sales were $170.7 million, 21.6% of net sales; total net sales fell from $6.01 billion in fiscal 2021 to $3.63 billion in fiscal 2025.
Sources: GameStop fiscal 2018 Form 10-K, fiscal 2025 and Q2 fiscal 2026 results releases.
